 Urban Meyer ‘seriously considering’ Maryland head coaching job, per report
 Meyer is "happy in his TV job but would like something to add a more positive page to the end of his resume" after the Jaguars debacle. 
 Credit: Adam Cairns/Columbus Dispatch 
 By Drew Lerner on 11/18/2026 11/18/2026 
 Less AI and more AA in your search results.
 Fox Sports college football analyst Urban Meyer is “seriously considering” becoming the head coach of the Maryland Terrapins.
 The news, first reported by Jeff Ermann of InsideMDSports , would bring to an end Meyer’s latest television stint as the star of Fox’s flagship college football studio show  Big Noon Kickoff . Meyer has not coached since his disastrous run with the NFL’s Jacksonville Jaguars, which ended in his mid-season firing. Since then, Meyer has stayed on television where he is the anchor of Fox’s college football studio. He has not shown any interest, at least publicly, of a return to coaching.
 Ermann reports that Meyer is “happy in his TV job but would like something to add a more positive page to the end of his resume” after the Jaguars debacle. He reportedly has “a warm relationship with Maryland athletic director Jim Smith” after the two men overlapped during Meyer’s successful stint at Ohio State.
 Meyer is now the second active television analyst to be tied to the Terps job. Reports have already indicated that former LSU and Notre Dame head coach Brian Kelly has interviewed for the gig, but Ermann reports he is “not expected to get the job.”
 Other candidates include Memphis coach Charles Huff, Indiana coordinators Mike Shanahan and Bryant Haines, and Maryland’s interim head coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim.
 With both Meyer and Kelly now tied to the position, it seems Maryland is going big-game hunting with its coaching search.
 Should Meyer depart Fox, the network could be in a position to completely overhaul  Big Noon Kickoff . The show has already shown signs of change this year, firing Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy midseason and recently opting to travel to sites that aren’t hosting the subsequent  Big Noon Saturday game.
 Without Meyer, the show would consist of host Rob Stone and analysts Matt Leinart, Mark Ingram, and Brady Quinn.
 While it’s far from certain Meyer would take the Maryland job, it’s the first indication that the College Football Hall of Fame inductee could have a final chapter left in him that isn’t in front of a television camera.
